23. PRECOCIOUS PUBERTY

•1:5000 – 1:10000
•Female to male ratio 10:1
•Development of SSC before age 8
•Development of breast or Pubic hair before age 7 in white girls and before age 6 in black girls.
⇨Puberty: is a complex process consisting of:
1.Maturation of hypothalamic – pituitary – gonadal (HPO) axis.
2.Appearance of SSC
3.Growth spurt.
4.Capacity for fertility.
5.Puberty can be:

Consonant – if it follows normal sequence.

Disconsonant – if it is abnormal.

•Puberty consists of physical changes.
•Adolescence consists of psychological and social changes.
•Puberty comes form 10 years onwards and usually takes 3 – 4 years with passage from one stage to another stage approximately every year.
⇨Thelarche: usually 1st sign of Puberty.
•Development of breast bud – tanner stage (2).
•Pubertal growth spurt occurs with breast budding, with peak velocity at mid puberty.
•Menarche occurs within 2 – 3years of thelarche median age for menarche 13 years.
⇨Pubarche: development of pubic hair followed by axillary hair. Pubarche follows thelarche.

Evaluation of child with precocious puberty:

History:

•Age of onset
•Sequence of events.
•Family history, mother, sisters.
•Neurological symptoms.
•Exogenous steroids.

Clinical Examination:

•Height, weight using age specific charts.
•BMI.
•Pubertal tanner stages.
•Neurological examination.
•Fundoscopy, visual fields.
•Skin lesions.
•Abdominal examination.
•External genitalia examination.
•Signs of virilization.

Biochemical tests and imaging:

•Given in table of comparison between CPP, PPP.

Treatment:

•Goals:
1.Halt or regression of SSC.
2.Prevent early menarche.
3.Retard skeletal maturation and improve height – growth hormone can be added.
4.Avoid psychological/ Behavioral/ sexual sequence.

Referral to: pediatric Endocrinologist.
